questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

While he went beside with our decisions, we were never sure he totally agreed.
questions.solution:
Ans: 1

Sol: The phrase ‘went beside’ does not have any meaning. ‘Went ahead’ means that something was carried out. The correct sentence is: ‘While he went ahead with our decisions, we were never sure he totally agreed.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The after morning (1)/ she woke to the first ray of (2)/ light through the window. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Ans: 1

Sol: The phrase ‘the after morning’ does not make any sense and renders the sentence grammatically incorrect. The correct sentence is: ‘The next morning she woke to the first ray of light through the window.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence ****given**** with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

The psychopath gets a ______________ sense of enjoyment from torturing animals.
questions.solution:
Ans: perverse

Sol: Perverse means inappropriate or unorthodox. It fits the sentence appropriately as the sentence then means that the sense of enjoyment that the psychopath gets from torturing animals is unorthodox and weird. Hence, ‘perverse’ is the correct word to fill in the blank.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

When Jaspal got angry, he started to ____________ his feelings with his hands.
questions.solution:
Ans: gesticulate

Sol: Gesticulate means use gestures, especially dramatic ones, instead of speaking or to emphasize one's words. It fits the sentence appropriately as the sentence then means that when Jaspal got angry, he started to make hand gestures to express his feelings. Hence, ‘gesticulate’ is the correct word to fill in the blank.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Fossilize
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Amalgamate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Fossilize"** means to become a fossil or to make something become a fossil; it can also imply becoming outdated or rigid in thinking. (जीवाश्म बनाना)

 
 
• **Example:** Over time, the bones fossilized and were preserved in the rock.
 
 
 
• **"Amalgamate"** means to combine or unite to form one organization or structure. (विलय करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The two companies decided to amalgamate to increase their market share.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the word similar in meaning to **'Fossilize'** is **'Amalgamate'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Amalgamate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Dissolve **(घुलना): To make a solid become part of a liquid.

 
 
• **Example:** Sugar dissolves easily in hot water.
 
 
 
• **Flex **(मोड़ना): To bend or move something, especially a muscle.
 
 
• **Example:** He flexed his muscles to show off his strength.
 
 
 
• **Liquefy **(तरल बनाना): To make or become liquid.
 
 
• **Example:** The heat liquefied the chocolate.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Depict
questions.solution:
Ans: Characterize

Sol: Depict means to represent by a drawing or painting or describe something. Characterize means to describe the distinctive features. Hence, the two words have similar meanings. Conceal means to hide, distort means to twist out of shape and suppress means to silence.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Differ
questions.solution:
Ans: Concur

Sol: Differ means to disagree, while concur means to agree. Hence, the two words have opposite meanings. Alter means to change, digress means to deviate and vary means to change.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Salve
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Blockage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"salve"** means a soothing balm or ointment used to heal or relieve pain. (मरहम)

 
 
• **Example: **She applied a salve to the burn to alleviate the pain.
 
 
 
• **"Blockage"** refers to an obstruction that prevents movement or flow. (अवरोध)
 
 
• **Example: **The blockage in the pipe caused the water to overflow.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'salve' **is **'blockage'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Blockage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Cerate **(मोम का लेप): A mixture of wax and fat used as a base for ointments.

 
 
• **Example:** The cerate was applied to the wound to promote healing.
 
 
 
• **Liniment **(मलहम): A liquid or lotion, especially one made with oil, for rubbing on the body to relieve pain.
 
 
• **Example: **He used a liniment to soothe his sore muscles after the workout.
 
 
 
• **Remedy** (उपाय): A medicine or treatment for a disease or injury.
 
 
• **Example:** Herbal tea is often used as a remedy for common colds.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase. **

Gnash your teeth
questions.solution:
Ans: Express rage

Sol: The phrase ‘gnash your teeth’ means to express a strong emotion, usually rage. Thus, Option 1 is the closest in meaning to the given phrase. An example sentence is: ‘After finding out about his rival’s promotion, Jack gnashed his teeth’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase. **

Let something slip through one's fingers

options.text: Not be able to understand a difficult concept
Let go of certain unpleasant things
To waste an opportunity to achieve something

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **"To waste an opportunity to achieve something"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• The phrase ‘let something slip through one’s fingers’ means an opportunity which was escaped or missed or to pass without being taken advantage of.

 
 
• **Example**: ‘I wouldn’t let such a wonderful opportunity slip through my fingers’.
 
 
 
• Hence option 4 is correct.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement". **

What would you like **(to do it)** for your birthday?
questions.solution:
Ans: to do

Sol: The word ‘it’ adds no meaning to the sentence and makes it grammatically incorrect. By removing it, the sentence becomes meaningful. The correct sentence is: ‘What would you like to do for your birthday?’

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

You must **(be mistake).**
questions.solution:
Ans: be mistaken

Sol: With the modal verb ‘must’, it is imperative to use the past participle form of the verb, ‘mistake’, which is ‘mistaken’. The correct sentence is: ‘You must be mistaken.’

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

Evidently, it was too

X -of a deadly-looking cobra or

Y -two we saw no reptiles

Z -dry for game, and with the exception
questions.solution:
Ans: ZXY

Sol: Z must be the starting sentence since the word ‘too’ is used to describe a quality, which only Z possesses, **‘dry’**. Thus, Z is the first sentence, which is seen only in Option 4, making it the correct choice.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

Some of these

X-height of more than

Y -2000 feet above the sea

Z -rocks rise to the
questions.solution:
Ans: ZXY

Sol: The opening sentence ends with ‘these’, referring to something. Sentences X and Y are linked together as they both refer to the height of something. Sentence Z contains ‘rocks’, which can be the reference. Hence, Z is the first sentence of the passage. This combination is seen only in Option 2, making it the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

I will wash the car every Sunday.

options.text: The car is washed by me every Sunday.
Every Sunday by me the car is to be washed.
Every Sunday by myself the car is to be washed.
The car will be washed by me every Sunday.

questions.solution:
Ans: The car will be washed by me every Sunday.

Sol: Sentences 2 and 3 change the structure of the sentence by making ‘every Sunday’ the subject of the sentence in the Passive voice when the subject is ‘wash the car’. Sentence 1 uses the present tense in the Passive voice while the Active voice uses the future tense. Only Sentence 4 preserves the tense and the structure of the sentence and correctly converts the voice.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

The watchman said, "Thief! Thief! Catch him!"

options.text: The watchman shouted to the crowd to catch the thief.
The watchman shouted to the crowd, thief, thief, catch him.
The watchman shouted to the crowd, catch the thief.
The watchman shouted to the crowd, thief, catch him.

questions.solution:
Ans: The watchman shouted to the crowd to catch the thief.

Sol: Sentence 2 directly converts into reported speech, without removing the exclamatory elements, Sentence 3 omits the use of ‘to’ before ‘catch’ and Sentence 4 does not contain any meaning in the reported speech. Only Sentence 1 correctly converts the exclamation of shouting and the verb into the reported speech and is the right answer.
